data.name: Sprocket.Term.LogicSystem
data.value: A ![](mark:logic-system) **logic system** is the automation for one machine, like an airlock. It holds [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term), the lists of steps it runs, and [![](mark:trigger) triggers](Term.Trigger class=term), which do a job when something happens.
data.comment: Codex page on "Logic system", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Installation
data.value: An ![](mark:installation) **installation** is a set of blocks and [![](mark:signal) signals](Term.Signal class=term) a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) works on, like one airlock among several.
data.comment: Codex page on "Installation", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.InstallationPanel
data.value: The **installation panel** is where you set up an [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term), selecting the blocks and [![](mark:signal) signals](Term.Signal class=term) for each of its [slots](Term.Slot class=term). Open it from the installation's row on the home screen. The [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term)'s `Installation panel` tab is where you choose what every panel shows.
data.comment: Codex page on "Installation panel", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Category
data.value: A **category** is a heading on the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel class=term) or a logic system's Sequences or Triggers tab that groups the [slots](Term.Slot class=term), [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term) or [![](mark:trigger) triggers](Term.Trigger class=term) dragged under it. A category of sequences can be set to run them one at a time.
data.comment: Codex page on "Category", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Slot
data.value: A **slot** is a named place in a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term), like the inner door, that each [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) fills with its own blocks or [![](mark:signal) signal](Term.Signal class=term). A required slot that is empty, or whose blocks were lost, is filled again on the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel class=term).
data.comment: Codex page on "Slot", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.LogicSystemStates
data.value: A [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term)'s ![](mark:state) **states** are what it remembers between jobs. Each [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) has its own. A state holds one value at a time. Most are on or off, and others, like an airlock's cycle state, hold a choice from a custom [state type](Term.Type class=term).
data.comment: Codex page on "Logic system states", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Type
data.value: A **state type** defines the values a [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) can have. For example, an airlock's "cycle" state might be *inside*, *cycling in*, *cycling out* or *outside*. Several states can use the same state type.
data.comment: Codex page on "State type", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Undo
data.value: ![](mark:undo) **Undo** takes back the last change, and ![](mark:redo) **redo** makes it again. Each [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) has its own history of changes, across all its screens, and the home screen has its own.
data.comment: Codex page on "Undo", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Sequence
data.value: A ![](mark:sequence) **sequence** is a list of [steps](Term.Step class=term) a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) runs from top to bottom. In an [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) it has to end before it can start again, so a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) that fires while it is running is missed.
data.comment: Codex page on "Sequence", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Step
data.value: A **step** is one line of a [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term). Press one of its parts to change it in a [selector](Term.Selector class=term), a menu or a panel.
data.comment: Codex page on "Step", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Action
data.value: An ![](mark:action) **action** is something a block can do, like opening a door or extending a piston.
data.comment: Codex page on "Action", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Option
data.value: An **option** is a value an [![](mark:action) action](Term.Action class=term) takes, like a piston's position and speed.
data.comment: Codex page on "Option", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Setting
data.value: A ![](mark:setting) **setting** allows you to adjust a logic system for each [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) without changing its steps, such as how long one airlock waits before it closes. It shows up on the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel class=term) alongside the other slots.
data.comment: Codex page on "Setting", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Expression
data.value: An **expression** is a value worked out from [![](mark:value) block values](Term.Value class=term), [![](mark:setting) settings](Term.Setting class=term) and [![](mark:state) states](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term), with +, -, × and ÷ and the functions min, max, round and abs. It is built on its own page by dragging calculations and values into place. A block value read from several blocks is combined as their sum, average, lowest or highest. It is worked out each time the [step](Term.Step class=term) using it runs. Make one with "Expression…", from a value's ![](mark:link) link mark or from the menu under the value a step sets a state to. A value that has to be fixed beforehand takes none: a state's starting value, a setting's default and an [installation](Term.Installation class=term)'s answer.
data.comment: Codex page on "Expression", shown in a tip on the line an expression is built in. It says what the term is, naming it in bold.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Task
data.value: A **task** is one operation: running or stopping a [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term), an [![](mark:action) action](Term.Action class=term) on blocks, or [setting](Term.Set class=term) a [![](mark:value) block value](Term.Value class=term).
data.comment: Codex page on "Task", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Value
data.value: A ![](mark:value) **block value** is a property of a block, like a light's color, which [steps](Term.Step class=term) can set or check.
data.comment: Codex page on "Value", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Awaitable
data.value: An ![](mark:awaited) **awaitable** is an [![](mark:action) action](Term.Action class=term) that goes on working for several [ticks](Term.Tick class=term), like a door closing, and that a [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) can [wait for](Term.Await class=term). Most actions are done at once, and of those that go on working, only the awaitables can be waited for.
data.comment: Codex page on "Awaitable", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Delay
data.value: A **delay** is a [step](Term.Step class=term) that pauses its [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) for a set time, in seconds or [ticks](Term.Tick class=term), like giving a sound time to play to its end.
data.comment: Codex page on "Delay", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Set
data.value: **Set** is a [step](Term.Step class=term) that gives a [![](mark:value) block value](Term.Value class=term) of some blocks a new value, like turning a light's power on. It is a [task](Term.Task class=term).
data.comment: Codex page on "Set", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Await
data.value: A **wait for pending tasks** is a [step](Term.Step class=term) that holds its [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) until the [![](mark:awaited) awaitables](Term.Awaitable class=term) above it have finished, like a door closing.
data.comment: Codex page on "Await", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Abort
data.value: An **abort** is a [step](Term.Step class=term) that ends its [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) at once. It can give a message saying why, shown as a note, a warning or a problem, and a problem also switches off the [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) it ran on.
data.comment: Codex page on "Abort", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one. "abort" is the step's word in the script, and note, warning and problem are its levels.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Catch
data.value: **if it fails** holds [steps](Term.Step class=term) that run when its [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) fails: a block can't do a step, or the sequence [aborts](Term.Abort class=term) with a warning or a problem. It doesn't run when the sequence is stopped, is switched off, or aborts with a note.
data.comment: Codex page on "if it fails", shown in a tip: the part of a sequence that runs when the sequence fails. It says what the term is, naming it in bold. "if it fails" is how the screen shows the script's catch.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Finally
data.value: **finally** holds [steps](Term.Step class=term) that run whenever its [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) ends, after **if it fails** where that ran, and when it is switched off too. While they run, the sequence shows as running, and stop ends them at once.
data.comment: Codex page on "finally", shown in a tip: the part of a sequence that runs however the sequence ends. It says what the term is, naming it in bold.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.If
data.value: An **if**, also known as a *conditional*, is a [step](Term.Step class=term) that checks blocks, or one of the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term)'s [![](mark:state) states](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term), and runs the steps under it only when its [condition](Term.Condition class=term) passes.
data.comment: Codex page on "If", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Condition
data.value: A **condition** is what an [if](Term.If class=term) checks, like a door being closed. If it fails, the [steps](Term.Step class=term) under it are skipped and the next [branch](Term.Branch class=term), if there is one, gets its turn.
data.comment: Codex page on "Condition", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Branch
data.value: A **branch** adds more [steps](Term.Step class=term) to an [if](Term.If class=term), run when the [conditions](Term.Condition class=term) above it fail. An `otherwise if` checks a condition of its own, and an `otherwise` runs when none above passed.
data.comment: Codex page on "Branch", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one. "otherwise if" and "otherwise" are the words of the branches on the screen, which stay English.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.RunAndStop
data.value: **Run** and **stop** are [steps](Term.Step class=term) that start or stop another [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) of the same [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term), in the same [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term). A sequence that is already running isn't started a second time.
data.comment: Codex page on "Run and stop", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Tick
data.value: A **tick** is the smallest step of time, sixty to a second.
data.comment: Codex page on "Tick", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Selector
data.value: A **selector** is the screen where you select what a [step](Term.Step class=term), an [if](Term.If class=term) or a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) works with, like its blocks and what to do with them.
data.comment: Codex page on "Selector", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Trigger
data.value: A ![](mark:trigger) **trigger** runs or stops a [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) when something happens, like a button being pressed. It fires only while its [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) and [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) are switched on.
data.comment: Codex page on "Trigger", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Signal
data.value: A ![](mark:signal) **signal** is what a block sends to fire a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term), from a slot on its toolbar or from a change in the block itself.
data.comment: Codex page on "Signal", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Library
data.value: The **library** contains your [![](mark:blueprint) blueprints](Term.Blueprint class=term), along with the [![](mark:logic-system) logic systems](Term.LogicSystem class=term) on this [construct](Term.Construct class=term) and [backups](Term.Backup class=term) of constructs that lost their automation.
data.comment: Codex page on "Library", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Backup
data.value: When a [construct](Term.Construct class=term) loses its last programmable block, each of its [![](mark:logic-system) logic systems](Term.LogicSystem class=term) with no [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) in the [library](Term.Library class=term) is saved there as a **backup**. Select it in the library and press `Add to this construct` to have it back.
data.comment: Codex page on "Backup", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Blueprint
data.value: A ![](mark:blueprint) **blueprint** is a copy of a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) saved in the [library](Term.Library class=term), ready to put on another [construct](Term.Construct class=term). It has no blocks of its own: each construct fills its [slots](Term.Slot class=term) with its own blocks.
data.comment: Codex page on "Blueprint", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Construct
data.value: A **construct** is a grid and everything pistons, rotors and hinges attach to it. A ship docked to a station by a connector or landing gear is a construct of its own: it isn't part of the station, and its blocks can't fill the station's [slots](Term.Slot class=term).
data.comment: Codex page on "Construct", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Back
data.value: Back
data.comment: Tooltip on the back arrow at the left end of the editor's heading bar, shown on every screen except the home screen. Pressing it returns to the screen before.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Close
data.value: Close the editor
data.comment: Tooltip on the close cross at the far right of the editor's heading bar, shown only on the home screen, where there is no screen to go back to. Pressing it closes the editor.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.PinHint
data.value: [Hold Alt to explore]{.hint}
data.comment: The line at the bottom of a tip that has terms in it. Holding the Alt key keeps the tip open and lights its terms, so the pointer can rest on one to open its tip. It is a span of the class hint, which draws it in the color terms light up in: a translation keeps the square brackets and {.hint} as they are.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Tips
data.value: Show fewer tips.
data.comment: Tooltip on the question mark in the editor's heading bar, shown while tips are on. Pressing it turns tips off, and the look of terms with them, in every world this player plays; the tips that stay are those on buttons that show only a mark and those saying why something cannot be pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.TipsOn
data.value: Show every tip.
data.comment: Tooltip on the question mark in the editor's heading bar, shown while tips are off. Pressing it turns every tip back on, in every world this player plays.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Undo
data.value:
[![](mark:undo) Undo](Term.Undo class=term)
{action}
data.comment: Tooltip on the undo arrow in the editor's heading bar, shown while there is a change to undo. {action} is one of the Sprocket.Change texts, filled in, such as Deleted step 3 in Cycle, "open Outer Door", and stands on its own line after the word Undo, or by Sprocket.Undo.Also holding that text where the undo takes changes on other screens along.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Redo
data.value:
[![](mark:redo) Redo](Term.Undo class=term)
{action}
data.comment: Tooltip on the redo arrow in the editor's heading bar, shown while there is an undone change to make again. {action} is one of the Sprocket.Change texts, filled in, such as Deleted step 3 in Cycle, "open Outer Door", and stands on its own line after the word Redo, or by Sprocket.Undo.Also holding that text where the redo makes changes on other screens again with it.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Broken
data.value: Something in it needs fixing. Open it to see what.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light is red because something in what the row opens needs mending.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Ran
data.value: It ran just now.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light flashes green just after the thing ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Idle
data.value: It is idle. Lights green when it runs, and red when something is broken.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light is dark: nothing ran a moment ago and nothing is broken.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOn
data.value: Switch this installation on
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while the switch is off, on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel. Shown only while the installation's logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOff
data.value: Switch this installation off and stop any running [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while the switch is on, on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel. Shown only while the installation's logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOn
data.value: Switch this logic system on, locking it against changes.
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has no installations, while it is off: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOff
data.value: Switch this logic system off, stopping its [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term) and unlocking it for changes.
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has no installations, while it is on: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOn
data.value: Switch on every [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) of this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term)
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has installations, while it is off: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens. Each installation then runs where its own switch is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintFirst
data.value: The [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) must be switched on first.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while its logic system is switched off and the installation's switch is dimmed and cannot be pressed: on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOff
data.value: Switch off every [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) of this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term)
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has installations, while it is on: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NameAbout
data.value: The name of this [construct](Term.Construct class=term), taken from its largest grid. Renaming it renames that grid.
data.comment: Tooltip on the construct's name in the home screen's heading: the name of its largest grid, the one with the most blocks. Pressing the name renames that grid.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NewAbout
data.value: Start a new [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) on this [construct](Term.Construct class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the home screen's button that adds a new logic system to the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.OpenInstanceAbout
data.value: Open the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel class=term) for **{name}**.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's row on the home screen, under its logic system; pressing the row opens that installation's installation panel. {name} is filled with the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprintAbout
data.value: Save a copy of this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) in the [library](Term.Library class=term) as a [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the button that makes a blueprint of a logic system, on its heading row on the home screen, and in the library on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, shown while the library holds no blueprint of the chosen logic system or backup.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.ChooseVersionAbout
data.value: Two [constructs](Term.Construct class=term) joined, each with its own version of {name}. Both stay switched off until you select one.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Choose a version button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen. {name} is the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateFromLibraryAbout
data.value: The [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) in the [library](Term.Library class=term) has more recent changes. Update the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) on this [construct](Term.Construct class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, that puts the library's newer blueprint in the logic system's place; shown where the blueprint was changed after the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateBlueprintAbout
data.value: Update the [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) from the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) on this [construct](Term.Construct class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, that brings the library's blueprint up to date from the logic system; shown once the library holds a blueprint and the logic system was changed after it.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.EditBlueprint
data.value: Opens the editor for the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) **{name}**.
data.comment: Tooltip on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and on the logic system's name in the editor's heading bar on the installation panel; pressing either opens the logic system's screen. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnotherAbout
data.value: Install the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) **{name}** on another set of blocks.
data.comment: Tooltip on the home screen's button under a logic system's installations that adds another installation. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.UseBlockAbout
data.value: The block this slot held is gone, and this one has the same name. Using it makes it the slot's block.
data.comment: Tip on the button that takes a block found by its name alone as the slot's own.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.OpenAbout
data.value: Name this slot and say what it is for.
data.comment: Tooltip on a slot's name in the slots list on a logic system's screen, while the logic system can be changed. Pressing the name opens the slot's panel, where it is named and described.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.NameAbout
data.value: This blueprint's name.
data.comment: Tip on a blueprint's name in the library, which it can be renamed on.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NameAbout
data.value: This logic system's name.
data.comment: Tooltip on a logic system's name in the editor's heading bar on its own screen, where pressing the name renames the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Delete
data.value: Delete this logic system, and every [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) of it
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin in the editor's heading bar on a logic system's screen, which deletes the logic system together with every installation of it.

data.name: Sprocket.System.DeleteInstallation
data.value: Delete this installation
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin of an installation's row on the home screen, which deletes that installation.

data.name: Sprocket.System.UsingAbout
data.value: Select the [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) whose blocks this screen shows. Blocks you select for a [step](Term.Step class=term) or a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) fill its [slots](Term.Slot class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the list of a logic system's installations at the top of its screen; the installation picked there fills the slots named in the screen's sentences.

data.name: Sprocket.System.TabFlagged
data.value: Something on this tab needs attention. The row with the problem says what.

data.value: Perform a [task](Term.Task class=term) when a block sends a [![](mark:signal) signal](Term.Signal class=term) or reaches a requested state.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EveryAbout

data.value: Select another [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term), or another value for it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names one of the logic system's states; pressing it opens the picker the trigger was made with.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Copy

data.name: Sprocket.System.CopyUnstarted

data.value: Open **{name}** to see and change its [steps](Term.Step class=term).

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Delete

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Copy

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.BlocksAbout
data.value: Select the block that fires this [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the block that starts it. Pressing the part changes the block.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.DoesAbout
data.value: Select what this [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) does.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the sequence it starts or stops. Pressing the part changes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.RateAbout
data.value: Change how often it should run.
data.comment: Tooltip on the length in an Every trigger's sentence on a logic system's screen, which says how often the trigger runs. Pressing it opens the length panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NameAbout
data.value: This sequence's name.
data.comment: Tooltip on a sequence's name in the editor's heading bar on its own screen, where pressing the name renames the sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomethingAbout
data.value: Perform an [![](mark:action) action](Term.Action class=term) on blocks or set a [![](mark:value) block value](Term.Value class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a task: an action on blocks, or setting one of their values.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Delete
data.value: Delete this sequence
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, and on the bin in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteStep
data.value: Delete this step
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin at the end of a step's row on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CopyStep
data.value: Duplicate this step.
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen. An if is copied with the steps in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ActionAbout
data.value: Select what this [step](Term.Step class=term) does.
data.comment: Tooltip on the action named in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the picker to choose what the step does.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.BlocksAbout
data.value: Select which blocks this [step](Term.Step class=term) acts on.
data.comment: Tooltip on the blocks named in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing them opens the picker to choose which blocks the step acts on.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OptionSlotsAbout
data.value: Select the target of this [![](mark:action) action](Term.Action class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the slots an action's option names in a sentence, such as where moving items takes them, on a sequence's screen and a logic system's screen; pressing them opens the selector of the target.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OptionsAbout
data.value: Change the [![](mark:action) action](Term.Action class=term)'s [options](Term.Option class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the options of an action, such as a piston's position and speed, in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen and in a trigger's sentence on a logic system's screen; pressing them opens the picker on the action's options.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NewValueAbout
data.value: Change the value to set.
data.comment: Tooltip on the new value in the sentence of a step or trigger that sets a value of blocks, on a sequence's screen and on a logic system's screen; pressing it opens the picker on that value.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ComparedAbout
data.value: Choose how it is compared.
data.comment: Tooltip on the comparison in an if's sentence on a sequence's screen, such as "is" or "is at least"; pressing it opens a menu of the comparisons the value can be checked with.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ReadAbout
data.value: Choose whether any or all of the blocks must pass, or whether their sum or average is checked.
data.comment: Tooltip on how an if reads its blocks where it names several: on the part of its sentence on a sequence's screen, and on the box over the column of blocks in the selector an if or a trigger on a number is made with. The choices are "any", "all / each", "the sum of" and "the average of"; the sentence says "all" as "each" where it reads a value, and pressing either opens a menu of them.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CheckedAbout
data.value: Change the value to check for.
data.comment: Tooltip on the value an if checks blocks for, in the if's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the picker on that value.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ReadWithAbout
data.value: Change what the [![](mark:value) block value](Term.Value class=term) is read with.
data.comment: Tooltip on what a value is read with, such as the button whose label it reads, straight after the value in the sentence of an if on a sequence's screen or of a trigger on a logic system's screen; pressing it opens the picker on it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.LengthAbout
data.value: Change how long the delay is.
data.comment: Tooltip on a wait step's length in its sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the panel where the length is given.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DragStep
data.value: Drag to move this step.
data.comment: Tooltip on the drag handle of a step's row on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.PauseStep
data.value: Pause this step. The [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) skips it until it is resumed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the pause mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen, while the step is not paused; pressing it pauses the step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.UnpauseStep
data.value: Paused: the [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) skips this step. Press to resume it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the pause mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen, lit while the step is paused; pressing it resumes the step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitTypedAbout
data.value: 60 ticks is one second.
data.comment: Tooltip on the number box where a timespan is typed: in the panel for a wait's length on a sequence's screen, the panel for a timer trigger's interval on a logic system's screen, and the column choosing how often a new timer trigger fires.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.RunsAbout
data.value: Select which [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) this [step](Term.Step class=term) runs.
data.comment: Tooltip on the sequence a run step names, on a sequence's screen, such as Cycle Out in "run Cycle Out". Pressing it opens the list of sequences to choose another.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.StopsAbout
data.value: Select which [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) this [step](Term.Step class=term) stops.
data.comment: Tooltip on the sequence a stop step names, on a sequence's screen, such as Cycle Out in "stop Cycle Out". Pressing it opens the list of sequences to choose another.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.WatchedAbout
data.value: Select which [![](mark:value) block value](Term.Value class=term) this [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) watches.
data.comment: Tooltip on the value a trigger on a number watches, on a logic system's screen, such as power in "when any power of Battery < 20". Pressing it opens the trigger's picker on the value.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.FillsAbout
data.value: Select what fills this [slot](Term.Slot class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on a slot's blocks, and on the signal beside them, on an installation panel. Pressing either opens the picker the slot is filled with.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.StepBlocks
data.value: Blocks this [step](Term.Step class=term) acts on:
data.comment: First line of the tooltip on the blocks of a step or an if on a sequence's screen, once it holds blocks, under the slot they come from; a list of them follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.TriggerBlocks
data.value: Blocks that fire this [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term):
data.comment: First line of the tooltip on the blocks a trigger watches, on a logic system's screen, once it holds blocks, under the slot they come from; a list of them follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.FromSlot
data.value: From the [slot](Term.Slot class=term) {slots}.
data.comment: In the tooltip on the blocks of a step or a trigger, over the line that heads the list of the blocks: the slot of the logic system the blocks fill. {slots} is the slot's name, in bold.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.SlotEmpty
data.value: It is empty in this [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term).
data.comment: In the tooltip on the slot a step or a trigger names, under the line naming the slot, where the installation shown has no block in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.FromSlots
data.value: From the [slots](Term.Slot class=term) {slots}.
data.comment: In the tooltip on the blocks of a step or a trigger, over the line that heads the list of the blocks, where they come from more than one slot. {slots} is the slots' names, in bold, separated by commas.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.ScreenOf
data.value: {block}: {screen}
data.comment: One line of the list in the tooltip on a slot of screens a step or a trigger names, on a sequence's screen and a logic system's screen: a block the installation shown fills the slot with, and the screen of it the slot holds. {block} is the block's name, {screen} the screen's name as the block calls it, such as Front.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.DoneAbout
data.value: Save any changes and go back.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar on a logic system's screen, a sequence's screen, the installation panel and a blueprint slot's screen, where every change is kept as soon as it is made.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DoneFirst
data.value: Select something in every column first.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar in the picker, and on the page choosing how often a timer trigger fires, while it cannot be pressed yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ClearTyped
data.value: Clear what is typed
data.comment: Tooltip on the cross at the end of a search box in the picker, which empties the box.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryKind
data.value: Show every kind again
data.comment: Tooltip on the cross beside the kind of block that the picker's column of blocks is narrowed to; pressing it shows every kind again.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ShowHidden
data.value: Show blocks hidden from toolbars
data.comment: Tooltip on the closed eye at the end of the heading of the picker's column of blocks; pressing it also lists the blocks set not to show in the toolbar config.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HideHidden
data.value: Hide blocks hidden from toolbars
data.comment: Tooltip on the open eye at the end of the heading of the picker's column of blocks; pressing it takes the blocks set not to show in the toolbar config out of the list again.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KindAbout
data.value: Show only one kind of block.
data.comment: Tooltip on the line in the picker's column of blocks that opens the list of kinds of block.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SourceAbout
data.value: Select what this works with.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Source box heading the first column of a selector, which chooses what the thing being made works with, such as blocks or a slot the logic system already has.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Waits
data.value: This is [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term). The [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) goes straight on while it works, and a `wait for pending tasks` [step](Term.Step class=term) below waits for it to finish.
data.comment: Tooltip on an awaitable action, one marked with the clock that works over several ticks: on its row in the selector and on its part of a sentence. Also the tooltip on a step's sentence on a sequence's screen when the step starts such an action and goes straight on. "wait for pending tasks" is the words of the step that waits, which stay English.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.RunAbout
data.value: Start the [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) selected below

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StopAbout
data.value: Stop the [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) selected below
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice at the top of the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes the trigger stop the sequence chosen in that column.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateFixedValueAbout
data.value: Use one of these values.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the label before the buttons for the state's own values, in the selector that sets, tests or watches one of the logic system's states.

data.value: Rename this state type
data.comment: Tooltip on a state type's name on a logic system's State tab, with its pencil. Pressing it lets the name be typed.

data.name: Sprocket.State.ChoiceAbout
data.value: Rename or remove this choice
data.comment: Tooltip on one of a state type's choices on a logic system's State tab. Pressing it opens a menu offering to rename or remove it.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateRenameAbout
data.value: Rename this state
data.comment: Tooltip on a state's name on a logic system's State tab, with its pencil. Pressing it lets the name be typed.

data.name: Sprocket.State.TypeRemove
data.value: Remove this state type
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a state type on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.TypeKept
data.value: A [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) uses this [state type](Term.Type class=term), so it cannot be removed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the dimmed bin beside a state type on a logic system's State tab, where a state holds one of its choices.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateRemove
data.value: Remove this state
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a state on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateKept
data.value: A [step](Term.Step class=term) or [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) uses this [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term), so it cannot be removed.

data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a state on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.HoldsAbout
data.value: Change the [state type](Term.Type class=term) of this [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term). Its starting value becomes the first value of the new one.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on what a state holds, after its name on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StartsAbout
data.value: The value the [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) has when the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) starts.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the words before a state's starting value, on the State tab and in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateNameAbout
data.value: Every [slot](Term.Slot class=term), [state type](Term.Type class=term) and [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) in a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) needs its own name.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the name of a new state in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.value: The [state type](Term.Type class=term) decides which values the new [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) can have.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.TypeNameAbout
data.value: Every [slot](Term.Slot class=term), [state type](Term.Type class=term) and [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) in a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) needs its own name.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the name of a new state type in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateValueOfAbout
data.value: Use whatever value another [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) has when this runs.

data.value: This uses [slots](Term.Slot class=term) the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) has already. Rename them on its `Installation panel` tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SlotMatchedOne
data.value: This uses a [slot](Term.Slot class=term) the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) already has. Press its name to rename it everywhere in the logic system.
data.comment: Tooltip on the picker heading while it shows, in italics, the name of the one slot the logic system already has that the blocks picked fill exactly, or that was picked by name with the Existing slot source. Pressing the name renames the slot everywhere.

data.value: The blocks selected replace this [slot](Term.Slot class=term)'s blocks in the [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) shown. Press its name to rename the slot everywhere in the [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the picker's heading while it shows the name of the slot a step or a trigger names, which the blocks picked will change because no slot holds them already. Where other steps or triggers use the slot too, Done asks whether to change it for all of them.

data.value: The blocks selected make a new [slot](Term.Slot class=term) with this name. Press the name to change it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the picker's heading while it shows the name of the slot the blocks picked will make, which no slot the logic system has fills exactly. Pressing it renames the slot before it is made; the name starts as the next numbered slot name.

data.value: This [slot](Term.Slot class=term) takes {kind} blocks.

data.name: Sprocket.State.KindKept
data.value: A [step](Term.Step class=term), [if](Term.If class=term) or [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) uses this [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term), so its [state type](Term.Type class=term) cannot be changed.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on what a state holds, on its row on a logic system's State tab, while a step or a trigger uses the state, so its state type cannot be changed.

data.value: The value this [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) has right now in the [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) shown. data.name: Sprocket.Slot.ShortAbout
data.value: The label shown on each button and toolbar slot that sends this [![](mark:signal) signal](Term.Signal class=term). Left empty, they show the [slot](Term.Slot class=term)'s name.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ForgetBackup
data.value: Forget this backup
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the bin at the end of a backup's row in the section of backups.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Forget
data.value: Delete it from storage
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the bin at the end of a blueprint's row in the section of blueprints kept in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.PutOn
data.value: Add to this [construct](Term.Construct class=term) as a [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term), with an empty [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) to fill.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes while a blueprint or backup is chosen: pressing it puts that one on the construct the editor was opened on as a logic system with one empty installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOff
data.value: Take this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) and its [![](mark:installation) installations](Term.Installation class=term) off this [construct](Term.Construct class=term).
data.comment: On the home screen, the tooltip on the minus in a logic system's heading row, shown where the logic system's blueprint is in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.AlreadyHere
data.value: This [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) is already on this [construct](Term.Construct class=term).
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, which puts a blueprint on the construct, while it cannot be pressed because the logic system of the chosen row is on the construct already, the same as its blueprint or with none.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Same
data.value: The [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) in the [library](Term.Library class=term) is the same as this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term).
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, which makes or updates a blueprint, while it cannot be pressed because the chosen logic system and its blueprint in the library are the same.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.InLibrary
data.value: This [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) is in the [library](Term.Library class=term) already.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, which makes or updates a blueprint, while it cannot be pressed because the chosen row is a blueprint kept in the library whose logic system is not on this construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.KeepsOne
data.value: A [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) needs at least one [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the dimmed bin of an installation's row on the home screen, shown when it is the logic system's only installation and so cannot be deleted.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.CopyAbout
data.value: Duplicate this logic system on this [construct](Term.Construct class=term).
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the copy mark in the strip between its panes: it puts a copy of the chosen logic system on this construct as a separate logic system. It can be pressed only while a logic system on this construct is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.PromoteAbout
data.value: Make this [backup](Term.Backup class=term) a [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term).
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes while a backup is chosen: pressing it makes the backup a blueprint in storage, no longer marked as a backup.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Deletes
data.value: Delete this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term), with its [![](mark:installation) installations](Term.Installation class=term). It has no [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) in the [library](Term.Library class=term), so this is its only copy.
data.comment: On the home screen, the tooltip on the bin in a logic system's heading row, shown where the logic system has no blueprint in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ResetAbout
data.value: Reset this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term) to its [![](mark:blueprint) blueprint](Term.Blueprint class=term) in the [library](Term.Library class=term). [![](mark:installation) Installations](Term.Installation class=term) keep their blocks.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, which puts the chosen logic system's blueprint back in its place, shown while the logic system has changed since that blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseIfAbout
data.value: Check another [condition](Term.Condition class=term) when none above passed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-branch menu on the row closing an if, on a sequence's screen, that adds an otherwise if branch.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseAbout
data.value: Run this when none of the [conditions](Term.Condition class=term) above pass.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-branch menu on the row closing an if, on a sequence's screen, that adds an otherwise branch.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.BranchAbout
data.value: Add a [branch](Term.Branch class=term) to this [if](Term.If class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the plus button on the row closing an if on a sequence's screen, which opens the menu of branches to add to the if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseTestAbout
data.value: Add a [condition](Term.Condition class=term) to this [branch](Term.Branch class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on an if's otherwise line on a sequence's screen that gives the branch something to check, which makes it an otherwise if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StateAbout
data.value: Select the [condition](Term.Condition class=term) that must pass.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of an if's sentence on a sequence's screen that says what it checks of its blocks, such as "is closed"; pressing it chooses another check.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SetStateAbout
data.value: Give one of this [![](mark:logic-system) logic system](Term.LogicSystem class=term)'s [![](mark:state) states](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term) a new value.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a step setting one of the logic system's states.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SystemStateAbout
data.value: Select another [![](mark:state) state](Term.LogicSystemStates class=term), or another value for it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a step's sentence on a sequence's screen that names one of the logic system's states; pressing it opens the picker the step was made with.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.EveryWorldAbout
data.value: Every world follows these settings where its own is left at `Default`. On a dedicated server they cover the worlds it hosts, and in your own game every world you play or host.
data.comment: In the admin settings, the tooltip on the tab for the defaults every world follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultAbout
data.value: Use the value set under Every world, and follow it if it changes later.
data.comment: In the admin settings, the tooltip on the first choice in each setting's list on the tab for this world, the choice that follows the value set on the tab for every world. Every world in the text is that tab's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AwaitAbout
data.value: Wait until every [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term) started above has finished.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a row waiting for every awaitable action started before it. ![](mark:awaited) draws the clock mark an awaitable action carries.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AwaitRow
data.value: The [![](mark:awaited) awaitables](Term.Awaitable class=term) started since the last `wait for pending tasks` run together, and the [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) waits here until all of them have finished.
data.comment: Tooltip on the words of a row waiting for every awaitable action started before it, on a sequence's screen. The row reads "wait for pending tasks", which stays English; ![](mark:awaited) draws the clock mark an awaitable action carries.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AbortAbout
data.value: End the [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) here.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice "abort" in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen, which adds a step ending the sequence at once. "abort" is the step's word in the script and stays English.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AbortPartAbout
data.value: Change the message and how it shows.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of an abort step's line on a sequence's screen that says its message and level, such as: saying "Door jammed" as a warning. Pressing it opens a small panel where both are given.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AbortLevelAbout
data.value: A note or a warning shows on the [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term). A problem also switches off the [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) it ran on, with the message as the reason.
data.comment: Tooltip on the three words "note", "warning" and "problem" in the small panel that opens from an abort step's line on a sequence's screen, which choose how the step's message shows when it ends the sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.RenameAbout
data.value: Rename this category
data.comment: Tooltip on a category's name, with its pencil, a heading among the slots on a logic system's Installation panel tab. Pressing it lets the name be typed.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Remove
data.value: Remove this category. Its [slots](Term.Slot class=term) stay, under no category.
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a category's name, a heading among the slots on a logic system's Installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.RemoveSequences
data.value: Remove this category. Its [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term) stay, under no category.
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a category's name on a logic system's Sequences tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.RemoveTriggers
data.value: Remove this category. Its [![](mark:trigger) triggers](Term.Trigger class=term) stay, under no category.
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a category's name on a logic system's Triggers tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AddBlocksAbout
data.value: Select blocks to make a new [slot](Term.Slot class=term) of, filled with them in this [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on "blocks" in the menu of the "+ slot" button on a logic system's installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AddSignalAbout
data.value: Select a signal, such as a button's press, to make a new [slot](Term.Slot class=term) of, filled with it in this [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on "a signal" in the menu of the "+ slot" button on a logic system's installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AddScreenAbout
data.value: Select a block's screen to make a new [slot](Term.Slot class=term) of, filled with it in this [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on "a screen" in the menu of the "+ slot" button on a logic system's installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AddInventoryAbout
data.value: Select a block's inventory to make a new [slot](Term.Slot class=term) of, filled with it in this [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on "an inventory" in the menu of the "+ slot" button on a logic system's installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AddSettingAbout
data.value: Make a new ![](mark:setting) [setting](Term.Setting class=term), a value each [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) gives for itself.
data.comment: Tooltip on "a setting" in the menu of the "+ slot" button on a logic system's installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.OpenAbout
data.value: Name this [setting](Term.Setting class=term), say what it is for, and change its default.
data.comment: Tooltip on a setting's name in the slots list on a logic system's installation panel tab, while the logic system can be changed. Pressing the name opens the setting's panel, as a slot's name opens the slot's: it is named and described there, and its default changed.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.ValueAbout
data.value: Choose the value this [![](mark:installation) installation](Term.Installation class=term) gives the [setting](Term.Setting class=term), or use its default.
data.comment: Tooltip on a setting's value on an installation panel. Pressing it opens the panel the installation's value is given in.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.HoldsAbout
data.value: What the [setting](Term.Setting class=term) holds. It is chosen when the setting is made.
data.comment: Tooltip on the label of what a setting holds, in the panel a setting is made or opened in.

data.name: Sprocket.Expression.ReadingAbout
data.value: Drop it where it goes, then select blocks and one of their [![](mark:value) block values](Term.Value class=term). Several blocks are always combined: as their sum, unless you choose average, lowest or highest.
data.comment: Tooltip on the "A reading…" button on the page an expression is built on. Pressing it opens the selector.

data.name: Sprocket.Expression.LowestAbout
data.value: The lower of the two values.
data.comment: Tooltip on the "lowest of" button on the page an expression is built on.

data.name: Sprocket.Expression.HighestAbout
data.value: The higher of the two values.
data.comment: Tooltip on the "highest of" button on the page an expression is built on.

data.name: Sprocket.Expression.RoundedAbout
data.value: The value rounded to the nearest whole number.
data.comment: Tooltip on the "rounded" button on the page an expression is built on.

data.name: Sprocket.Expression.WithoutSignAbout
data.value: The value without its minus sign, so -5 becomes 5.
data.comment: Tooltip on the "without sign" button on the page an expression is built on.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Open
data.value: Rename this category, or have its [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term) run one at a time.
data.comment: Tooltip on a category's name on a logic system's Sequences tab. Pressing it opens a panel with the category's name and the "One at a time" switch.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.OneAtATimeAbout
data.value: Where it is on, only one [![](mark:sequence) sequence](Term.Sequence class=term) in this category runs at a time. A start while another one runs is missed.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.OptimizeAbout
data.value: Reduce the [slots](Term.Slot class=term) to as few as the [steps](Term.Step class=term) and [![](mark:trigger) triggers](Term.Trigger class=term) need.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Optimize slots button on the installation panel tab of a logic system's screen, at the right end of the SLOTS heading, while the logic system is switched off and the slots can be changed.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.RemoveAbout
data.value: Remove this unused slot.
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a slot no step, if or trigger names, on the installation panel and on the Installation panel tab of a logic system's screen, while the logic system is switched off. Pressing it removes the slot, with every installation's blocks in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Drag
data.value: Drag to move the category with its [slots](Term.Slot class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a category's name, a heading among the slots on a logic system's Installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.DragSequences
data.value: Drag to move the category with its [![](mark:sequence) sequences](Term.Sequence class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a category's name on a logic system's Sequences tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.DragTriggers
data.value: Drag to move the category with its [![](mark:trigger) triggers](Term.Trigger class=term).
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a category's name on a logic system's Triggers tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Drag
data.value: Drag to move the slot. At the bottom of a [category](Term.Category class=term), drag right to put it in or left to leave it out.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a slot's name on a logic system's Installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Drag
data.value: Drag to move the sequence. Drop it above a [category](Term.Category class=term)'s end to put it in.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a sequence on a logic system's Sequences tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Drag
data.value: Drag to move the trigger. Drop it above a [category](Term.Category class=term)'s end to put it in.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a trigger on a logic system's Triggers tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.ExpectsAbout
data.value: The kind of block that can fill this [slot](Term.Slot class=term). Press it to choose another.
data.comment: Tooltip on the type of block a block slot takes, under the Expects label in the slot's panel. Pressing it opens a picker listing the types the slot can take, wider or narrower, down to one kind of block; only those offering everything the slot's steps and triggers do with it.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.MarkupAbout
data.value: Show the guide to writing rich text.
data.comment: The tooltip on the button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen that opens the guide to formatting text.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Open
data.value: Opens the door. This is [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term).
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "open" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Close
data.value: Closes the door. This is [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term).
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "close" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Reverse
data.value: Opens a closed door and closes an open one.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "reverse" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.AnyoneCanUse
data.value: When on, anyone can open and close the door, not only those the owner shares the block with.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "anyone can use" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.ToggleAnyoneCanUse
data.value: Switches `anyone can use` on when it is off, and off when it is on.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "toggle anyone can use" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.AutoCloseDelay
data.value: How long the door stays open before it closes by itself.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "auto close delay" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.HowFarOpen
data.value: How much of the way the door has opened, from 0 % when closed to 100 % when fully open.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "how far open" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Open.Status
data.value: Met while the door is fully open.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "open" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Closed
data.value: Met while the door is fully closed.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "closed" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Opening
data.value: Met while the door is opening, and while a door that lost its power partway stands where it stopped. Once it is fully open, the status is `open`.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "opening" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.Closing
data.value: Met while the door is closing, and while a door that lost its power partway stands where it stopped. Once it is fully closed, the status is `closed`.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "closing" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.FinishesOpening
data.value: Fires a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) when the door is fully open.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "finishes opening" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.FinishesClosing
data.value: Fires a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) when the door is fully closed.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "finishes closing" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.StartsOpening
data.value: Fires a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) when the door starts to open.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "starts opening" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Door.StartsClosing
data.value: Fires a [![](mark:trigger) trigger](Term.Trigger class=term) when the door starts to close.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "starts closing" of a door, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Extend
data.value: Extends the piston all the way out to its maximum distance. This is [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term).
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "extend" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Retract
data.value: Retracts the piston all the way in to its minimum distance. This is [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term).
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "retract" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.MoveTo
data.value: Moves the piston to a position. This is [![](mark:awaited) awaitable](Term.Awaitable class=term).
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "move to" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Reverse
data.value: Reverses the piston's `velocity`, so it moves the other way.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "reverse" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.AddPistonHead
data.value: Adds a head to the piston.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "add piston head" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Velocity
data.value: How fast the piston moves, in meters per second. A positive velocity extends it and a negative one retracts it.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "velocity" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.MinimumDistance
data.value: The shortest distance the piston retracts to, in meters.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "minimum distance" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.MaximumDistance
data.value: The longest distance the piston extends to, in meters.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "maximum distance" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.MaximumImpulseAlongTheAxis
data.value: The most force the piston may push with against an obstacle in the direction it extends.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "maximum impulse along the axis" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.MaximumImpulseAcrossTheAxis
data.value: The most force the piston may push with against an obstacle sideways, across the direction it extends.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "maximum impulse across the axis" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.SafetyDetachDistance
data.value: How far the head can be pushed out of place before it detaches from the piston, in meters.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "safety detach distance" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.ShareInertiaTensor
data.value: When on, the masses of the grids the piston joins are evened out, for steadier behavior.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Position

data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "position" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Extending

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.Retracting
data.value: Met while the piston is retracting.
data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "retracting" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.comment: Codex entry on the block member "stopped" of a piston, shown in the picker when it is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Piston.FinishesRetracting
